concerns.text: Imputation (mean for near‑symmetric variables, median for skewed variables) can alter distributional shape, directly affecting both Type I error and power estimates, yet the design provides no sensitivity analysis or control for this confound (e.g., comparing results with and without imputation). This threatens the validity of the claimed impact of transformations.

The bootstrap confidence‑interval half‑width target of ≤ 0.02 assumes sufficient precision from the aggregated estimates. Given the strict filtering (≥ 50 raw datasets, but many may be excluded) the effective sample size may be far lower, making the precision requirement potentially unattainable and rendering the inference under‑powered.

Aggregating per‑dataset error‑rate estimates and applying a Friedman test treats each proportion as an independent observation, ignoring the within‑dataset variance of the permutation‑based error estimates. A hierarchical or mixed‑effects model would more appropriately account for this nested uncertainty; the current approach may yield anti‑conservative significance tests.
